text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's National Security Service warned against attempts by local business conglomerates to undermine a restrictive currency board regime aimed at stabilising the economy.
-- The European Investment Bank may extend some 60 million Ecus for the reconstruction of the Sofia Airport, the airport's executive director Danyo Adanev said. @
-- Bulgaria's private Cantek company, which sells Canon office equipment said it held a 34 percent share of the local market last year with sales worth of 740 million levs.
-- A lev/mark exchange rate of 1,000 was assumed in Bulgaria's draft budget for 1997, Finance minister Muravei Radev said.
-- Last year Bulgaria posted $76.7 million deficit in its trade with the former Soviet republics, now members of the Commonwealth of Independent States, private Balkan agency said. @

-- Bulgaria's State Savings Bank (SSB) chairman Bistra Dimitrova said she would not resign before a check into SSB operations by the central bank supervision department was completed. Dimitrova has said earlier she would resign by the end of last week.

-- Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) executive council said it had decided to ban senior UDF officials from sitting on commercial companies' boards in a bid to prevent possible corruption charges against them. @
-- Foreign investments in Bulgaria since 1990 totalled only $830 million because of long delayed reforms and high crime rate, National Statistics Institute figures showed.
-- Bulgaria posted a curent account deficit of $22.3 million last year after a $25.6 million gap in 1995, Bulgarian National Bank figures showed.
-- Possible failure of the introduction of a currency board system in Bulgaria will result in Albania-style destruction of state institutions, Bulgaria's prime minister Ivan Kostov said.
